title: Notify the warden when the month's invoices are generated
description: Raised while auditing what Lodgy actually notifies about, and confirmed by the PO as a gap rather than a deliberate silence. InvoiceGenerationWorker runs daily and creates the month's invoice for every active agreement on its billing cycle day, and posts nothing - a grep for notification calls in that worker returns zero. So the one event that creates the warden's work for the month happens invisibly, while overdue rent and recurring expenses both notify. The warden's first sign that invoices exist is opening the Payments tab and finding them, which means the collection cycle starts whenever they happen to look rather than when it actually begins. SHAPE: one summary notification per generation run, not one per invoice - a hostel with thirty tenants must not produce thirty notifications. Something like 'March invoices ready - 12 invoices, ₹60,000 due', tapping through to the invoice list. Reuse the existing dues channel rather than adding a third, since it is the same audience and the same switch should govern it; if the PO wants it separately toggleable that is a third channel and should be said explicitly. A run that generates nothing must stay silent.
acceptanceCriteria: When the generation worker creates one or more invoices, the warden gets a single summary notification for that run
The notification says how many invoices were created and the total amount due, not just that something happened
Tapping it opens the invoice list
A run that creates no invoices posts nothing at all
Many invoices in one run still produce exactly one notification, never one per invoice
It respects the existing payments-and-expenses switch, so a warden who turned that off is not notified
Generation itself is unchanged - this only adds the notification, and an invoice is still created exactly once per agreement per period

history.note: Filed after the PO confirmed that silent invoice generation is a gap. Specced as one summary notification per run rather than per invoice, on the existing dues channel.

Built. InvoiceGenerationWorker now counts what it created and posts a single summary - 'This month's invoices are ready - N invoice(s) generated, Rs X due in total' - on the existing dues channel, so the same switch governs it and no third channel appears. Tapping it opens the Payments tab. Note on the route: I used LodgyDestination.Payments.route ('payments') rather than inventing an 'invoices' route, which the NavHost does not know and which would have made the tap a no-op; it is also allow-listed in isSupportedNotificationRoute so the exported-activity validation from LODGY-46 still passes it. A run that creates nothing posts nothing, and generation itself is unchanged - invoices are still created exactly once per agreement per period. New strings in both locales. TESTS: 3 new - one summary for a three-invoice run rather than three notifications, silence when nothing is created, and the dues switch suppressing the notification while still generating the invoices. Full suite 434 pass, coverage 96.98% line. Not schema-affecting.

PASS with one honest gap. The three unit tests are the substance here and they cover the criteria directly: a three-invoice run posts exactly one notification, a run that creates nothing posts nothing, and turning the payments switch off suppresses the notification while still generating the invoices. I also verified the route by reading it rather than trusting it - ROUTE_INVOICE_LIST is LodgyDestination.Payments.route ('payments'), not an invented 'invoices' route the NavHost would not resolve, and it is allow-listed in isSupportedNotificationRoute so the LODGY-46 exported-activity validation still accepts it. That was the most likely way to ship a notification whose tap does nothing. THE GAP, recorded rather than glossed: I did not see this notification fire on the device. Generation only runs on an agreement's billing cycle day, which is the 5th for this test data, and the clock was at the 15th after the vacancy testing; landing on it would have meant another month's jump. The dues and vacancy notifications from the same session both fired correctly, so the posting mechanism itself is proven - what is unverified on device is specifically the generation-day trigger. Worth one confirmation when someone is next on a real device.
